metaDescription: Oak Hills, Butler County mineral rights owner? We buy fractional oil and gas interests near this legacy oil-and-gas region, honest cash offers, no pressure.
heroLead: Oak Hills sits in Butler County, a place with oil and gas history that goes back well before Marcellus shale, where family farms have carried mineral rights through generations of shallow well leases and, more recently, deeper Marcellus development.
intro: Butler County has a layered history most people outside the area don't know about — this is legacy oil country as much as it's modern shale gas country, and it's common for a single family tract near Oak Hills to have an old shallow well from the 1970s or 80s sitting alongside a modern Marcellus unit boundary. We've untangled that kind of dual history for other owners and can do the same for you before we ever talk numbers.

sections.heading: Two Layers of History Under One Tract
paragraphs: If your family's Oak Hills property has an older shallow well that's stopped producing or produces very little, that doesn't mean the deeper Marcellus rights under the same acreage are worthless — the two are often leased and valued separately, and a shallow well going dry has no bearing on what the deep rights are worth if the tract sits inside an active wet-gas unit.

We check both layers when we review a Butler County tract, because owners are sometimes surprised to learn they're getting shortchanged on the deeper rights while assuming their mineral interest is tapped out because the old well stopped paying.

sections.heading: What Determines Your Offer
paragraphs: We look at recent royalty history if there's an active lease, unit boundaries recorded with Butler County, and how close your tract sits to producing pads nearby. Any value we quote is hedged to that activity, not a flat number, because two tracts a half mile apart in Butler County can differ significantly depending on unit participation.
If your interest has never been leased, we can still make an offer, priced against what unleased minerals in similar Butler County tracts have recently changed hands for.

faqs.question: My family has an old shallow oil well on the property. Does that affect the mineral sale?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Shallow rights and deep Marcellus rights are often leased separately, so a depleted shallow well doesn't mean the deeper rights have no value.

faqs.question: How do you determine my fractional share?
faqs.answer: We trace the recorded deed chain through the Butler County recorder of deeds to confirm exactly what percentage you hold before quoting a number.

faqs.question: Is there any cost to get an offer?
faqs.answer: No, our review and offer are both free, whether or not you decide to sell.
